questions.q: Why does ad hoc, tribal-knowledge IT support tend to break down as an organization grows past a handful of staff?
options: Each team starts inventing its own definitions of urgency and escalation, producing inconsistent service for the same kind of request
Tribal knowledge actually improves automatically with more staff
Larger organizations no longer experience any IT incidents
Growth has no effect on how consistently IT support is delivered
questions.explain: Without a shared framework, consistency depends entirely on who happens to be on shift, which breaks down once teams, shifts, and locations multiply.

questions.q: What does the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) require of publicly traded companies with respect to IT, per this lesson?
options: A specific ITSM software vendor must be used
Effective, auditable internal controls over systems affecting financial reporting, including documented change management
All IT staff must hold an ITIL certification
IT incidents must be resolved within one hour
questions.explain: SOX requires evidence of a documented, auditable trail for changes to systems affecting financial reporting — not a specific tool or certification.

questions.q: What is MTTR, and how does a formal incident management process typically affect it?
options: MTTR is a certification exam, and ITSM has no effect on it
MTTR is the number of open tickets, and ITSM increases it
MTTR is mean time to resolution, and defined triage, escalation, and a knowledge base tend to reduce it
MTTR is a security vulnerability scanner used in change management
questions.explain: MTTR is the average time to restore service after an incident; triage criteria, a known escalation path, and documented history of past fixes shorten it without adding headcount.

questions.q: What is ISO/IEC 20000, as described in this lesson?
options: A U.S.-only tax regulation unrelated to IT
A ticketing software product
The international standard for a service management system, against which organizations can be independently certified
The fourth version of the ITIL framework
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 20000 is a certifiable international standard for service management systems, distinct from any specific framework version or tool.

questions.q: Why does a shared ITSM framework help when an organization adopts a new commercial tool or brings in an outside managed service provider?
options: It eliminates the need for any vendor or tool altogether
It guarantees the new tool will be free of defects
The new tool or vendor already shares the same vocabulary for incidents, problems, and changes, so it can plug into existing processes instead of starting from zero
It has no real effect on how new tools or vendors integrate
questions.explain: A common framework gives every tool and vendor the same definitions of incident, problem, and change, so new additions map cleanly onto existing processes.
